name: nukewar
label: Possibility of an all-out atomic war

questions.text:
I'm going to read you some possible military situations the U.S. might face in the next ten years. (HAND CARD BB) 
Some people feel these situations are certain to happen (think of these as point 7 on the scale), others think these situations won't happen at all (think of these as point 1 on the scale). And of course some people have opinions somewhere in between. For each of these possible military situations, please give me your best guess as to how likely it is to happen. For example, an all-out atomic war. Where would you put the likelihood of an all-out atomic war during the next ten years? (Would you say 7--it is certain to happen, 1--it won't happen at all, or something in between?) 
(CIRCLE ONE CODE FOR "A" AND REPEAT FOR B-F)
A. An all-out atomic war?

name: knwforgn
label: Level of R's information: foreign policy

questions.text:
We want to ask about how much information you have on various topics. Please look at Card B21. For each of the following areas, please indicate whether you are very informed, somewhat informed, neither informed nor uninformed, somewhat uniformed, or very uninformed about the issues. 
A. Foreign policy
questions.stem: We want to ask about how much information you have on various topics. Please look at Card B21. For each of the following areas, please indicate whether you are very informed, somewhat informed, neither informed nor uninformed, somewhat uniformed, or very uninformed about the issues.

name: intintl
label: Interested in international issues

questions.text: International and foreign policy issues. Are you very interested, moderately interested, or not at all interested?

name: moretrde
label: More trade, less jobs in usa

questions.text: Suppose two friends of yours are talking about trade with other countries. One friend thinks that increased trade has created a lot of jobs in the United States for people with jobs like yours. The other friend thinks that increased trade has taken away a lot of jobs in the United States for people with jobs like yours. Which view is closer to your own?

name: ldcgap
label: Differences between rich and poor too large

questions.text:
Turning to international differences, do you agree or disagree: 
A. Present economic differences between rich and poor countries are too large.
questions.stem: Turning to international differences, do you agree or disagree:
questions.item: A. Present economic differences between rich and poor countries are too large.

name: ldctax
label: Rich countries pay tax to help poor countries

questions.text:
Turning to international differences, do you agree or disagree: 
B. People in wealthy countries should make an additional tax contribution to help people in poor countries.
questions.stem: Turning to international differences, do you agree or disagree:
questions.item: B. People in wealthy countries should make an additional tax contribution to help people in poor countries.
